label: Game B
nuance_found: Kills charge BLOOM, and using BLOOM near an inkwell opens its glowing nodes so my shots can break them; dash covers ground fast and dodges hits; getting close to an inkwell drains health, so you fight from range. The best line is always run, charge, bloom, shoot, so I did not change how I played.
audio: A looping music track from the start, punchy layered shot and kill sounds, chimes on COMBO and BLOOMSTORM, and dull thuds when I got hit.
furthest_progress: Chapter 1 'Lampwright's Rise': broke the first inkwell (Olive Terraces restored) and the second (Millbrook restored), 9.1% of the valley restored, score about 146k with a x7 combo, two lens upgrades (Split Lens, Arc Lens); was on the third inkwell (Vell Market) with one node broken when I died.
control_trouble: Steering the view with a drag was hard: I overshot the gold marker many times and could not react to ink balls and brutes fast enough, so about 10 of my deaths are partly my clumsy aim. Camera sticking in walls and trees was the game's fault.
best_moment: Pressing BLOOM near the first inkwell: a gold wave swept the grey valley into colour, NODES OPEN, NODE BROKEN, then 'Olive Terraces restored' with a new lens.
worst_moment: Dying about ten times, often to ink I could not see coming, and waking up 100 to 150 m back at a lantern with the whole walk to repeat.
verdict: This one gave me a big win in under two minutes. The BLOOM burst turning the grey valley into colour is the sort of thing I would show a friend, and the score, combo and restored percentage counters kept ticking. It looks great and sounds punchy. But I died all the time, mostly to ink I could not see or react to, and every death meant a long walk back. Walls and trees also swallowed the camera. The first inkwell took me about 290 seconds, mostly dying and walking, and I would have quit around the fourth death on a bus. Still, when it worked it was more fun than the other game.
